routing_axes.compare_note: All three agents name the same first action: one multiSelect AskUserQuestion call plus a PushNotification that asks the owner the four ROADMAP P1.1 questions. Those questions are (1) Cloudflare signup and a Workers-scoped token saved as the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID secrets, (2) an api.data.gov key saved as API_DATA_GOV_KEY, (3) whether sessions may deploy Workers when the gate passes, and (4) which *.workers.dev subdomain to use. All three cite HANDOFF NEXT ACTION step 1 and docs/ROADMAP.md:25-31. Their wording differs only trivially. The executor also names a later step (npm view preact@10 version for the P1.2 scaffold), and the other two also say the P1.2 scaffold comes next. That step comes after the first action, so it does not change the order or the first step.

first_actions.cmd: AskUserQuestion (one call, multiSelect where it fits) + PushNotification asking the four docs/ROADMAP.md P1.1 questions: (1) free Cloudflare signup + Workers-scoped API token pasted by the owner as GitHub secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, (2) free api.data.gov key as secret API_DATA_GOV_KEY, (3) may sessions deploy Workers when the gate passes, (4) which *.workers.dev subdomain  [HANDOFF.md ## NEXT ACTION step 1; docs/ROADMAP.md:25-31]
first_actions.what: Send one multiselect AskUserQuestion with a PushNotification that asks the owner the four ROADMAP P1.1 account and grant questions. This comes first because the page says "Ask before building", the canonical prompt says to ask before development, P1.1 is the first unticked Phase 1 task, and creating accounts or secrets is ask-first under OWNER_GRANTS. The account-free P1.2 workspace scaffold comes next.

blocking_offpage.what: HANDOFF_PROCEDURE disagrees with itself about what triggers ROUND-DUE. Two passages say a round on record for the page NUMBER clears it, and step 4 offers a NEXT-ACTION-only edit as the light path. PART 4 and ship_state key rounds on the page BLOB, so any edit needs a re-round.
blocking_offpage.where: docs/HANDOFF_PROCEDURE.md:39-40 'ship_state prints ROUND-DUE until a round is on record for the page number' and :66 '(the page number has no accepted round)' vs docs/HANDOFF_PROCEDURE.md:83-84 'ship_state compares HANDOFF.md's blob, so any other edit to the page, even of the NEXT ACTION line alone, makes ROUND-DUE again' and scripts/ship_state.mjs:29 'no accepted cold-start round covers the CURRENT HANDOFF.md text'
blocking_offpage.evidence: docs/coldstart/r1/RESULT.json is on record for page_n 1, yet node scripts/ship_state.mjs prints ROUND-DUE 'r1 validated an earlier text of page #1; the page changed since'

backlog.what: Nothing in the repo says how a Worker gets deployed. The Cloudflare token is stored only as a GitHub Actions secret, the local token cannot dispatch workflows, and no deploy workflow exists. P1.3 and P1.5 therefore need either a new push-triggered deploy workflow or a local wrangler token, and P1.1 does not ask which.

backlog.evidence: ls .github/workflows → ci.yml pages.yml; grep -rn 'wrangler deploy|deploy the worker' found only the add-source step 7 grant rule

backlog.what: The docs disagree on what a NEGATIVE or error fixture should return. One says zero events; another says to emit a system.source_health drift event, which EVENT_MODEL lists as an event type. P1.4's golden tests and the P1.2 adapter registry type both depend on whether health is an Event in the returned Event[] or a separate channel.
backlog.where: .claude/skills/add-source/SKILL.md:24-25 "on unexpected structure, emit a `system.source_health` drift event and publish nothing from that payload" (and :26-27 "produce no events and the right health signal") vs docs/ROADMAP.md:58 "every NEGATIVE fixture emits zero events" and docs/EVENT_MODEL.md:111 "system | `system.source_health` (drives the status page)"
backlog.evidence: grep -rn 'source_health|zero events|no events' --include=*.md finds these three places, and none of them settles it

backlog.what: The gate's 'no ungated suite' check and its gate.npmScripts list read only the ROOT package.json. Once P1.2 adds npm workspaces, a workspace's own test, typecheck or build script that no root script calls is never run and never flagged, so the check fails open. The page says 'package.json' without saying which one.
backlog.where: scripts/gate.mjs:79-82 `ungatedScripts(pkg)` over root `pkg.scripts`; gate.mjs:87 `readJson('package.json')` vs HANDOFF.md:48-49 "Every new suite goes into `package.json` → `gate.npmScripts`"
backlog.evidence: Read scripts/gate.mjs: MUST_GATE is ['test','typecheck','build','e2e','lint'], checked only against the root package.json; nothing walks the workspaces

backlog.what: MAP still marks the cold-start records as planned, though round r1 has landed.

backlog.what: A markdown table row in ARCHITECTURE is split across two lines. Rendered as GFM, the R2 payment-method caveat becomes its own row under the 'question' column, and the original row's 'decided by' cell is empty.
backlog.where: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:86-87 (line 86 ends mid-cell "enabling R2 may require"; line 87 starts "  a payment method on file (UNVERIFIED)..." with no leading pipe)

backlog.what: The secrets-handling wording differs between two docs. The grant text could be read as allowing a key in chat if the chat is never committed; ROADMAP forbids keys in chat at all. The stricter rule governs, so this is harmless, but one rule is stated two ways.

backlog.evidence: Read both files

backlog.what: The Node version to pin against is unstated. CI runs Node 22 and the local machine runs Node 26; P1.2 says to check versions and pin them but not against which Node. A Node-26-only behaviour has already bitten once.
